items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] It’s interesting also that there have been a number of jazz musicians who have been good amateur painters, like Ellington, like Miles, Pee Wee Russell. [INTERVIEWEE] It is true, yes.

ctx.x: Again, he just – the way he talked about art was just – it wasn’t music. He didn’t know anything about music. He loved it and loved us and loved jazz, but it was his way of explaining how an artist – how he thought. I’ve always gotten a lot out of reading the autobiographies of artists. I had Vincent van Gogh, letters to Theo, I recommend – I was just telling one of the young guys. I said, get that book, because that is about revealing the process. When you see the process – especially when you see it away from –…
It’s interesting also that there have been a number of jazz musicians who have been good amateur painters, like Ellington, like Miles, Pee Wee Russell.
It is true, yes. Tony Bennett. Yeah, there’s something . . .
